unit.title: From Reduction Rules to a Tested Lambda-Calculus Evaluator
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student beginning deliberate software-engineering practice
prerequisites: Comfort with recursion, trees, sets, and asymptotic reasoning
Ability to write and run unit tests in one locally available programming language
Basic familiarity with variable binding and functions
learning_objectives: Translate a small-step operational semantics into modular executable code
Implement free-variable analysis and capture-avoiding substitution
Make fresh-name generation and evaluator outcomes deterministic
Separate semantic logic, execution limits, tests, and user-facing evidence
Use focused tests to expose binding, evaluation-order, stuck-term, and fuel-boundary defects

included: A named abstract syntax tree for the untyped lambda calculus
A fuel-bounded driver with explicit Value, Stuck, and OutOfFuel outcomes
Unit, boundary, and interaction tests plus concise engineering documentation
excluded: Static type checking or type inference
De Bruijn indices and compiler optimization
WebAssembly, ownership, async Rust, session types, and final projects
Any claim of completing an official Stanford assignment or the full CS242 course

unit_completion_requires: A runnable implementation of every operation named in STUDY_TASK.md
A deterministic automated test suite covering every required behavior class
A reproducible local test command and captured result summary
A short decision record explaining representation, freshness, and result-state choices
Learner-authored responses to every prompt in COMPREHENSION.md
completion_policy.evidence_rule: Files, captured commands, and validator results are evidence; a prose declaration of completion is not.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: Completing this kickoff can mark only managed_unit_01_lambda_evaluator complete. The course remains in progress until later, separately sourced units are admitted to the graph and independently validated.

derivation_basis: The snapshot describes classic lambda calculus and an interpreter/type-checker assignment among the course topics.
The snapshot identifies OCaml and Rust as course languages but does not provide retrieved lesson or assignment bodies.
The manager bounded the kickoff to an implementation-language-neutral evaluator so it is self-contained and assessable without pretending to reproduce an official assignment.
